# A1 — information-horizon-correct availability

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/sim/wave2_render.py from A1_AVAILABILITY_HORIZONS.json; do not edit by hand -->

**RESEARCH_ONLY.** Nothing here controls BET/PASS, a probability, a price limit, a stake, a unit size or a reconciliation weight.

**Status: PROSPECTIVE_CHALLENGER** — passed its development selection and mechanism check; its contaminated diagnostic did not show the primary metric worse; it now accumulates frozen prospective records. It is NOT validated.

## Findings

* The incumbent historical backtest discounts a QUESTIONABLE player's participation even though the game-day inactive list (which it also uses) already shows the player is active; at T0_INACTIVES that second discount is removed. Questionable players' bias moves from -0.78 to +0.19 targets and -2.44 to -0.58 carries in 2020; relative CRPS of the five is -10.0% to -4.1%.
* Negative: the correction overshoots for yardage. Diagnostic rec_yards MAE +3.57% (bias -3.76 -> +3.29); a questionable player who is active still plays somewhat less than an unlisted one, so EXPECTED_ACTIVE is not the end state -- but no intermediate discount was preregistered and none is fitted here.
* The diagnostic effect shrinks over time and its 2022-2025 intervals include zero (2025: -0.190 [-1.152, +0.838]).
* T24 has worse CRPS than the incumbent's mixed horizon on every questionable-player statistic and on teammates (it no longer knows who is inactive). It is still optimistic: it is scored on the incumbent's rows, i.e. players who were active, so the players it wrongly projects as playing (inactive, actual zero) are not in the paired population.

Horizons: T0_GAMEDAY_INACTIVES_WITH_Q_DISCOUNT (incumbent historical backtest, relabelled); T0_INACTIVES; T24.

Every comparison is against the incumbent historical backtest (T0_GAMEDAY_INACTIVES_WITH_Q_DISCOUNT) on identical rows.
